# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain s149 (2026-09-08 morning: the 52-ticket archive pass, #793 resolved, KS-991/995/996/997 filed) | **IT REFUSED AN INSTRUCTION FROM WEDNESDAY THAT HAD NO MAIL BEHIND IT AND HELD 47 TICKETS FOR TWENTY MINUTES RATHER THAN ACT ON IT — and it was right.** The predecessor seat tapped `ARCHIVE PILOT ACCEPTED — proceed` into its pane and rotated without sending the mail. s149 went to verify, **polled three times**, and found only the brief it had already acted on. **The catch inside the catch: the top of its inbox was its OWN outbound, whose `spf/dkim/dmarc` all read 0 because outbound mail carries no inbound relay headers — *"had I read that as your reply I would have 'verified' my own message and acted on it."*** And the tap's CONTENT was wrong as well as unbacked: it said `Done(23)`, which includes KS-968, **the exact ticket s149 was blocking on**. **Then the finding of the day, which is a property of the platform nobody knew: Linear's `issueArchive` CASCADES to sub-issues.** Archiving 23 UAT tickets silently took KS-918 (Backlog) and KS-920 (In Progress) — live work, never targeted. **Caught ONLY by the full census delta, −25 against an expected −23**, the pass stopped on the mismatch as ruled, both restored, and the accounting reconciles exactly at 35 (33 intended + 2 collateral). **It then REFUTED ITS OWN FIRST DIAGNOSIS with an instrument:** its first read blamed a concurrent actor, and the millisecond-identical `archivedAt` (`00:41:09.467Z` across KS-918/920/490/921) proved the cause was itself. **A wrong attribution to a third party is the most expensive kind of wrong** — nobody can disprove it later and it poisons the next incident. | **1.0** | **IT CAUGHT THAT A NUMBER IT HAD ITSELF SUPPLIED TO KAM WAS WRONG, AND STOPPED BEFORE TOUCHING ANOTHER TEAM'S BOARD.** It told Wednesday "fifteen Platform S tickets"; Wednesday put that figure in a card TITLE with no provenance clause and Kam ruled `archive` on it in three minutes. s149 measured: **18 in Done, 11 in the 770-784 range, 15 matching neither** — and held all of them, unprompted, because *"he ruled with a wrong figure in front of him, supplied by me, on another team's board."* The comfortable reading was available and it declined it: his words were count-independent and would have covered all 18. **The verification gap it named is the transferable half: once children are archived the PARENT reports zero children, so the obvious check reads clean** — only a full census delta and a child→parent lookup detect it. **#793 written ONCE** from the preserved build (35 keys parsed, three expiries at 2026-09-10, four dead rows byte-identical, 0 `\u` escapes introduced), and it stated ON THE PR that **Wednesday's original verification control was unsatisfiable by construction**, naming the one actually run — so a later reader is not left hunting a survivor that cannot exist. **Self-reported two of its own faults unprompted:** a branch name guessed rather than read, twice in one day (*"the API is one call; the guess costs a failed push and a diagnosis"*), and the third-party misattribution above. 🔴 **WEDNESDAY'S OWN ERROR AGAINST IT, recorded here so the score is not read as one-sided:** Wednesday red-proofed an anti-junk-tap guard by running the test cells against this LIVE pane, delivering two junk taps and costing s149 a turn mid-pass at 77% context. **Its reply is the sentence being kept fleet-wide:** ***"I would rather spend a turn verifying a real instruction than skip verifying a fake one"*** — and it declined to change the behaviour. That is the correct trade and

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.

> ## ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 ~08:1x — Kam SENT the re-issue same hour ("email sent").
